UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

                                                          )
Southwest Power Pool, Inc.                                )                      Docket No. ER26-247-000
                                                          )

                                           COMMENTS OF
                                        ENCHANTED ROCK, LLC

        Pursuant to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”)’s

October 27, 2025 Combined Notice of Filings #1 in the above-captioned proceeding,1 Enchanted

Rock, LLC (“Enchanted Rock”) hereby submits these comments (“Comments”) for the

Commission’s consideration. Enchanted Rock generally supports and commends Southwest

Power Pool (“SPP”)’s efforts to establish procedures that facilitate the expedited, flexible, and

cost-effective interconnection of large loads through SPP’s proposed High Impact Large Load

(“HILL”) and HILL Generation Assessment (“HILLGA”) tariff provisions (together, the

“HILLGA Proposal”).2 However, as discussed further below, Enchanted Rock respectfully

requests: 1) that the Commission require an additional, minimal modification to SPP’s HILLGA

Proposal, and 2) that the Commission accept the HILLGA Proposal, subject to a minimal future

compliance obligation by SPP to codify Enchanted Rock’s proposed minimal modification,

consistent with the Commission’s authority under, inter alia, Section 205 of the Federal Power

Act (“FPA”)3 and NRG Power Marketing, LLC v. FERC.4


1
  Southwest Power Pool, Inc., et al. Combined Notice of Filings #1, Docket No. ER26-247-000, et al. (Nov. 14,
2025).

Letter.” Capitalized terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the same meaning set forth in the SPP Proposed
Tariff or Filing Letter, as applicable.

4

2017) (per curiam); order on remand, PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 161 FERC ¶ 61,252 (2017).
 I.      ABOUT ENCHANTED ROCK

        Enchanted Rock is a leading microgrid developer, owner, and operator headquartered in

Houston, Texas, with over 1.5 GW of natural gas generation operational and under construction

for critical facilities and large loads. With more than 370 sites commissioned or contracted across

the country, Enchanted Rock delivers dependable power solutions to data center, manufacturing,

hospital, water, utility, and additional large load customers with a combined 99.9998% reliability.

Through its on-site generation solutions, Enchanted Rock offers “speed to power” for large load

facilities, which aligns with the HILLGA Proposal. Enchanted Rock’s on-site generation also

serves as a transitional mechanism to bridge existing transmission constraints and future

infrastructure buildouts, providing flexibility during transmission planning and operations.

II.     EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

        The rapid growth of data centers, efforts to develop and reshore U.S. manufacturing, and

the expansion of crypto mining operations, inter alia, have created an inflection point with

respect to U.S. economic development and national security. The growth of these heavily energy-

dependent industries is central to maintaining American technological leadership and de-risking

global supply chains, placing the interconnection of large, energy-intensive loads at the center of

our country’s national interest.

        The Secretary of Energy’s recent letter5 to the Commission requesting it to initiate an

Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking6 proceeding, and the Commission’s subsequent request




5
  See Interconnection of Large Loads to the Interstate Transmission System, Secretary of Energy’s Direction that the
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Initiate Rulemaking Procedures and Proposal Regarding the
Interconnection of Large Loads Pursuant to the Secretary’s Authority Under Section 403 of the Department of
Energy Organization Act, Docket No. RM26-4-000 (Oct. 23, 2025).
6
  See Interconnection of Large Loads to the Interstate Transmission System, Secretary of Energy’s Proposed
Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, Docket No. RM26-4-000 (Oct. 23, 2025) (“ANOPR”).


                                                         2
 for comments on the Secretary’s ANOPR proposal,7 demonstrate the importance of addressing

the interconnection of large-load facilities. Existing load and generation interconnection

frameworks were not designed to prioritize the influx of large load facilities within the timelines

required to maintain U.S. economic and energy dominance, highlighting the need for a

comprehensive framework that streamlines large load interconnections, while preserving

reliability, affordability and regional flexibility. Enchanted Rock views SPP’s HILLGA

Proposal, as well as SPP’s anticipated future proposal to introduce certain Conditional High

Impact Large Load Service (“CHILLS”) tariff provisions,8 as key to furthering the Commission’s

and the Department of Energy’s goals.

        Large load customers, particularly data centers and affiliated upstream manufacturing

facilities (including manufacturers of semiconductors, microchips, servers, and server

components) are seeking commercially available options that facilitate “speed to power” while

maintaining reliability. Enchanted Rock previously submitted comments to the Commission in

support of a “Load Co-located with Dispatchable Generation Option” (“LCDG Proposal”),

whereby “load and generation may be separately metered but are studied together for purposes of

retail load interconnection and integration, transmission and resource adequacy planning, and

operations.”9

                                                       3
         Enchanted Rock views SPP’s HILLGA Proposal as similar in many respects to Enchanted

Rock’s LCDG Proposal, with both proposals enabling speed to power for large load customers.

Similar to Enchanted Rock’s LCDG Proposal, the HILLGA Proposal would facilitate accelerated

interconnection timelines for co-located load and generation, and offer a flexible, on-site

generation solution that mitigates transmission constraints and resource adequacy risks for

existing customers on the grid.

        That said, Enchanted Rock respectfully requests that the Commission require SPP to

slightly modify its HILLGA Proposal to reflect realistic generation capacity accreditation

parameters that would account for the technical and commercial realities of serving HILLs

reliably under limited transmission service, as discussed further, infra, Section III.

III.    RECOMMENDED REVISIONS TO HILLGA PROPOSAL

        As indicated, Enchanted Rock generally supports and commends SPP’s initiative to

establish a framework for the creation of a new HILL transmission customer class and generally

supports the HILLGA Proposal, albeit subject to a minor modification to reduce barriers for new

generation interconnection10 through adjustments to one of the HILLGA Proposal’s eligibility

and requirements provisions.11 More specifically, Enchanted Rock recommends that the

Commission and SPP consider an expansion to the proposed parameters related to a generation

facility’s projected capacity accreditation value.12




10
   As stated, Enchanted Rock also looks forward to SPP’s anticipated CHILLS proposal as an essential complement
to HILLGA, which will further encourage flexibility and speed for large load facilities.
11
   See Filing Letter, Section III.B.1; SPP Proposed Tariff, Attachment BB (“Eligibility and Requirements
Provisions”).
12
   See Filing Letter at 26; SPP Proposed Tariff, Attachment BB, Section 3.1.3.


                                                       4
            SPP’s HILLGA Proposal currently provides that the projected capacity accreditation MW

value of any generation facilities submitted in a HILLGA Request(s) must not exceed the

associated HILL’s requested load, multiplied by the greater of:

           1) 110% plus the Planning Reserve Margin outlined in the HILLGA Study Agreement;
              or

           2) 125%.13

           However, these values are not representative of actual on-site generation capacity

requirements given customer requirements for generation availability. Notably, it is standard

industry practice for generation facilities to be oversized relative to their associated HILL

demand value to build in redundancies for generator failures. In Enchanted Rock’s experience,

large load customers’ targeted availability rates range from 99.9% to 99.999%, which require

significant oversizing of on-site generation, while back-up-only, on-site configurations require

approximately 25% excess on-site capacity to ensure reliable service.

           Importantly, when dispatched for grid-synchronized operations for load management and

market participation, Enchanted Rock’s technology deployments can remain at or below 110% of

nameplate load. That is, Enchanted Rock’s solutions can enable a large load customer to be

flexible while staying below SPP’s aforementioned capacity accreditation ceiling. However, on-

site generation facilities operating under temporary prime power arrangements (i.e., those that

utilize “bridging power” until full transmission service can be provided) require upwards of 30%

to 50% additional capacity to meet customer availability requirements. These arrangements can

be in place while infrastructure (e.g., network upgrade) buildouts are ongoing, and/or while the

HILL facility awaits firm transmission service.




13
     See SPP Proposed Tariff, Attachment BB, Section 3.1.3.2.


                                                          5
                Moreover, excess generation from an on-site generator supporting bridging power for a

large load customer is not initially intended for export to the grid, but should be eligible to

transition to Network Resource Interconnection Service (“NRIS”) or Energy Resource

Interconnection Service (“ERIS”) once the HILL’s Load Limited Resource Interconnection

Service (“LLRIS”) expires. The HILLGA Proposal’s current capacity accreditation construct

effectively prevents this excess generation from being studied within the LLRIS framework, and

therefore, any generation above the capacity accreditation cap is excluded from transitioning to

ERIS or NRIS, and from eventually providing firm, reliable power to the grid.

               Accordingly, Enchanted Rock respectfully requests that the Commission accept the

HILLGA Proposal, subject to a condition that SPP amend Attachment BB, Section 3.1.3.2 of its

Proposed Tariff in a future compliance filing, such that the projected capacity accreditation MW

value of any generation facilities submitted in a HILLGA Request(s) may not exceed the

associated HILL’s requested load, multiplied by the greater of: 1) 110% plus the Planning

Reserve Margin outlined in the HILLGA Study Agreement; or 2) 150%, rather than the

currently proposed 125% value.14 Enchanted Rock believes that this slightly higher capacity

accreditation cap will ensure that many on-site power solutions are not unnecessarily restricted

from being able to meet the HILLGA Proposal’s broader goals, while also recognizing the extent

to which many on-site power solutions must be oversized in order to meet large load customers’

availability needs in the short term.

               Accordingly, adopting Enchanted Rock’s proposal will ensure that valuable generation

capacity that can leveraged to support robust resource adequacy and grid reliability is not

stranded, will facilitate on-site power solutions that can support the timely energization of large

                                                      6
 load facilities that cannot afford to wait for lengthy transmission expansions before they can

begin operating, and will support the broader policy goals of the Commission and Department of

Energy. Moreover, Enchanted Rock’s minor proposed change to the HILLGA Proposal is the

type that is within the Commission’s authority to suggest to SPP when otherwise accepting a

filing made pursuant to FPA Section 205.15

IV.        CONCLUSION

           Enchanted Rock appreciates the opportunity to provide these Comments and as stated,

commends SPP for advancing pathways to promote the timely and reliable interconnection of

large load facilities.
